code.originalText: Primary care follow-up three weeks after starting immunosuppressive therapy, with a cataract and eye review

text.paragraph: Three-week review on immunosuppressive therapy, and glare in the right eye. [S]

Madame Curie returns three weeks after starting horse antithymocyte globulin, cyclosporine, eltrombopag, and acyclovir. She completed the four-day antithymocyte globulin course. She takes cyclosporine twice daily, eltrombopag on an empty stomach away from dairy, and acyclovir twice daily, and has missed no doses. She has had no fever, chills, sore mouth, rash, or joint pain, and no new bleeding beyond occasional bruises. She still tires by midafternoon and is writing at home on shortened days. Glare from the right eye makes small print and night driving difficult, and it is slowing her reading. [S]

Severe aplastic anemia: pancytopenia with a low reticulocyte count, confirmed by a hypocellular bone marrow; attributed to cumulative occupational ionizing radiation; linked to the documented 1842 diagnosis
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; the 1934 report remains D and the radiation cause is R.

S — Synthetic modern coding of the documented exposure history.

list.item:
Severe aplastic anemia, three weeks into immunosuppressive therapy (D61.2). No infection or bleeding. Counts have not yet risen, as expected this early: hemoglobin 8.2 g/dL, neutrophils 0.5, platelets 21, reticulocytes 18 thousand per microliter. Creatinine has risen from 0.78 to 0.96 mg/dL (eGFR 65) and potassium is 4.8 on cyclosporine; ALT 28 on eltrombopag. [S]
Continue cyclosporine, eltrombopag, and acyclovir.
Ask hematology today for a cyclosporine trough with the next counts and a dose review against the creatinine rise.
Weekly blood counts with the hematology day unit; transfuse if symptomatic or hemoglobin falls below 7 to 8 g/dL.

Posterior capsule opacification, right eye (H26.491). Glare and blurred reading in the right eye after earlier cataract surgery are limiting her reading and night driving. [S]
Refer to ophthalmology for a comprehensive dilated eye examination and laser capsulotomy if it confirms the cause.
